newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Axa, UAP to create world insurance giant.
newsitem.headline: French Axa, UAP to create world insurance giant.

text.p: French insurance companies Axa and UAP said on Tuesday they would ally to create an "unrivalled" group.

The companies, second and third biggest in Europe in terms of turnover behind Allianz AG Holding of Germany, said in a joint statement that the alliance plan would be submitted to the boards of the two companies on Tuesday.

They gave no details of the plan in their statement but said they had asked stock exchange authorities to suspend trading in their shares. A UAP spokesman said a news conference was being planned for later in the day.
French newspapers said a UAP-Axa alliance would create the world's biggest insurance company.
Talk of an Axa takeover has been pushing UAP shares up on the Paris stock exchange recently. The UAP share closed at its highest level since early March on Friday, up 6.27 percent at 116.90 francs.
UAP was privatised in 1994 at 152 francs a share and hit a high of 160 francs in July of the same year before a decline in the share.
Axa, whose stock closed on Friday at 318.5 francs, has a strong presence outside France, notably in the United States, where it owns Equitable and National Mutual in Australia.

Axa reported first-half net attributable profit of 1.977 billion francs on turnover of 87.5 billion francs, while UAP emerged from a two-billion-franc loss in 1995 to produce a first-half 1996 net attributable profit of 860 million francs.
